options: A desktop-only application that doesn't run in a browser
A command-line tool that must be installed separately
A billing statement emailed once a month
The web-based interface at portal.azure.com for creating, viewing, and managing Azure resources
questions.explain: The Azure Portal is the browser-based UI where you'll do most of your day-to-day work before you're comfortable with the CLI or automation tools.

questions.q: What does the Favorites section of the side menu let you do?
options: Permanently delete services you no longer want to exist
Automatically create new resources without any configuration
Pin the services you use most for one-click access, instead of browsing All services every time
Change the pricing of a service
questions.explain: Favorites lets you shortlist exactly the services you use, dragging them in or out of the menu as needed.

questions.q: What is the keyboard shortcut for the Azure Portal's global search bar on Windows?
options: Ctrl+Shift+Esc
F5
Ctrl+Alt+Delete
Ctrl+/
questions.explain: Ctrl+/ (Cmd+/ on Mac) opens the global search bar, which jumps straight to a service, resource, or documentation topic by name.

questions.q: What is a resource "blade" in the Azure Portal?
options: The panel that opens when you view a specific resource, showing its Overview, Settings, and configuration options
A type of virtual machine size
A physical piece of server hardware
A billing category unrelated to any specific resource
questions.explain: Every resource type opens its own blade with a consistent pattern — Overview at the top, then Settings and more specialized options below.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why is it worth building the habit of using global search early on?
options: Search is required to create any resource at all
Menus are removed from the portal entirely after your first login
Search only works for resources created in the last 24 hours
Once you've created more than a handful of resources, searching is almost always faster than navigating menus to find one
questions.explain: As the number of resources you've created grows, searching by name becomes faster than clicking through menu categories to find the right one.
